traceSteps.2: Sam asks for a mortgage in principle.
traceSteps.3: Sam's agent finds lenders through the index and looks North Bank up on the register.
traceSteps.4: The agents describe themselves and Sam's agent applies.
traceSteps.5: North Bank says what evidence it needs.
traceSteps.6: Sam's agent asks Harbour Bank for a signed balance statement.
traceSteps.7: Harbour Bank asks for a stronger approval.
traceSteps.8: Sam does a face check and the request is sent again.
traceSteps.9: Harbour Bank returns a signed statement with its terms.
traceSteps.10: Sam's agent checks the statements it holds.
traceSteps.11: Sam is asked, and the agent shares the evidence.
traceSteps.12: North Bank's gate checks the evidence.
traceSteps.13: North Bank returns a signed decision in principle.
traceSteps.14: Each side checks its own record.
traceSteps.25: The valuer requests the agreed fee
traceSteps.30: Sam approves the exact payment order

solid-provider.name: The fictional independent Solid storage provider

standIns.replacedBy: A fictional provider with its own key stores opaque signed bytes in memory. LDN description reads, POSTs, listings and reads use guarded in-process HTTP; WAC checks verified request identities. The provider sees every read. Every party is fictional.

Pinned fictional request signatures authenticate method, target, body digest, headers, time and nonce. A fixed public-address DNS stand-in routes only to the in-process provider; this is not Solid-OIDC.

branches.what: The storage operator alters a posted message before its receiver reads it.

solid-provider.name: The fictional independent record storage provider

standIns.replacedBy: A fictional separately keyed Solid provider, independent of the agent operator, holds signed copies of the real ledger. Sam can read them with Sam’s own key. In-process guarded HTTP and WAC replace network storage. All parties are fictional.
The outage branch makes the provider unavailable at disclosure approval, then returns it after the evidence gate has held the action. Recovery timing is controlled by the fictional host.

branches.what: The independent record store goes down before application evidence leaves; the evidence gate holds the action until storage returns.

solid-provider.name: The fictional Solid access-rule storage provider

standIns.what: Solid access rules and expiry scheduling
standIns.replacedBy: A separately keyed fictional provider enforces WAC on a balance resource. A fictional provider timer withdraws the read ACL at expiry; WAC itself has no date condition. The ordinary signed terms still control downstream purposes and copying. All parties and HTTP exchanges are fictional and in process.

branches.what: The proposed access-rule translation includes Write; the data terms gate refuses before any grant is applied.

solid-provider.name: The fictional WebID profile storage provider

standIns.what: WebID profile hosting and public DNS
standIns.replacedBy: A separately keyed fictional Solid provider serves Sam’s and the lender’s agent and principal profiles in memory. SDK Controlled Identifier publication and resolution use guarded, bounded, redirect-refusing in-process HTTP. A fixed public-address DNS mapping replaces network DNS.

A separately keyed fictional register signs only WebIDs, verification-method names, thumbprints and explicit key lifetimes. It supplies no public keys and conveys no authority to act. All parties are fictional.

branches.what: The lender profile publishes a different key while its independently signed register thumbprint remains unchanged.
